title: Rice–Shapiro and finite positive evidence

based_on.title: Basic Computability Theory
based_on.pages: 1993, revised 2013; §3.3 Definition 3.3.1 and §3.3.1 Theorem 3.3.3(1), with its finite-witness remark; printed pp.33–36, PDF pp.43–46

summary: Recognizable extensional properties of partial programs are exactly those supported by an effectively enumerable family of finite positive observations.
abstract: Seeing a program return seventeen supplies a reason to accept it as a program that can return seventeen. Seeing no return on an input supplies no comparable reason to conclude that it will never stop. Rice–Shapiro makes this difference precise for properties that depend only on the partial function computed by a program. Such a property has a recognizer exactly when its positive instances can be certified by finite tables of observed input and output pairs, drawn from an effectively enumerable family. Every program extending an accepted table must still have the property. Self-reference proves both the extension requirement and the existence of a finite accepted table. The characterization explains why specified successful outputs can be recognized, while totality and an exact finite domain cannot.
